1_executive_technology_brief.what_it_does: Converts intracranial pressure (ICP) into a chemical molecular signal in CSF, detectable by a wearable biosensor — eliminating all electronics, batteries, and RF from the intracranial implant.
1_executive_technology_brief.why_it_matters: Current ICP monitors require batteries (replacement surgery) and electronics in the brain (infection risk, RF interference). This platform eliminates all intracranial electronics.
1_executive_technology_brief.technical_differentiator: Genuinely new communication channel: chemical molecular signaling through CSF. No prior implant uses chemistry instead of electronics for ICP monitoring.

2_mechanism_dossier.causal_chain: ICP changes → mechanical deformation of implant transducer → release rate of synthetic molecule changes proportionally → molecule transported through CSF → wearable biosensor detects concentration → ICP reconstructed remotely
2_mechanism_dossier.operating_states: Normal ICP: baseline release. Elevated ICP: increased release (proportional to pressure). Decreased ICP: decreased release.

subsystems: ICP-responsive molecular release transducer (implant, zero electronics)
Signal reconstruction algorithm (converts concentration to ICP)

4_engineering_specification.molecule: UNSPECIFIED — requires medicinal chemistry program to design: ICP-proportional release, CSF biocompatibility, wearable-detectable specificity, metabolic inertness, clearance half-life suitable for ICP monitoring (minutes-hours). Status: MISSING.
4_engineering_specification.transducer: Mechanical-to-chemical transducer. ICP deforms a membrane, changing release rate. Status: HYPOTHESIS.
4_engineering_specification.sensor: Wearable biosensor detecting target molecule at nanomolar concentration in CSF-equilibrated interstitial fluid. Status: HYPOTHESIS.

5_prototype_blueprint.v1_prototype: Bench-top: pressure chamber + molecular release device + sampling + concentration assay. Prove ICP-to-concentration relationship.
5_prototype_blueprint.what_to_build_first: Design the molecule. Without a specific molecule, no prototype is possible. This is a medicinal chemistry task, not an engineering task.

7_experimental_protocol.test_2: CSF transport: prove molecule reaches detectable concentration at lumbar/subcutaneous site within clinically useful time.
7_experimental_protocol.test_3: Wearable sensor: prove detection at target concentration with required specificity.
7_experimental_protocol.test_4: Chronic: prove molecule is biocompatible, metabolically inert, and stable over >5 years.

existing_evidence.claim: No prior art found for molecular ICP signaling

cost_removed.source: Industry estimates for implantable battery replacement

sensitivity_analysis.base_case: 100K patients × $20K/surgery ÷ 7.5 years = $267M/year avoided cost. Package $500K = 0.002x annual avoided cost.

known_adjacent_technology: CGM (continuous glucose monitoring — different molecule, different physiology)

10_ip_differentiation_dossier.honest_disclosure: This is the HIGHEST-RISK, HIGHEST-DIFFERENTIATION package. The molecule is UNSPECIFIED. The architecture is novel but UNVALIDATED. The buyer is purchasing a concept + architecture + design path, NOT a validated product.

11_regulatory_standards_map.likely_classification: Class III (implantable). Novel mechanism — likely requires De Novo or PMA.
unresolved_questions: How does FDA classify a chemical-signaling implant?
What safety data is needed for chronic molecular release into CSF?

12_manufacturing_transfer_plan.estimated_development_path: Molecule design (12-24mo) → Bench prototype (6-12mo) → Pre-clinical (24-48mo) → Clinical (36-60mo) → PMA (24mo). Total: 8-14 years to market.

hazards: Molecule toxicity (unknown — molecule not designed yet)
Release failure (no ICP data — same as no monitor, not unsafe)
Sensor failure (no data — fallback to standard external ICP measurement)
13_safety_package.safe_states: If system fails → patient has NO ICP monitoring (same as no implant). Must NOT interfere with standard shunt drainage.

14_integration_package.how_it_plugs_in: Transducer integrated into shunt reservoir. Wearable sensor is separate device. No modification to shunt drainage function.
